rules.name: Unescaped HTML marked safe via Markup()
rules.description: A value is wrapped in markupsafe.Markup() (or jinja2.Markup()). This marks the string as trusted HTML and disables auto-escaping, so any dynamic content is rendered verbatim into the response.
rules.remediation_example:
from markupsafe import escape
return render_template('page.html', body=escape(user_body))

rules.name: Template source built from dynamic input (render_template_string)
rules.description: render_template_string() (or a direct Jinja2 Environment.from_string() call) receives a template whose source is assembled from dynamic values. The value becomes template source, so it can include new template tags and markup that bypass auto-escaping of the outer template.

rules.name: Auto-escaping explicitly disabled
rules.description: Template auto-escaping is turned off (autoescape=False) or HTML output is returned with mark_safe/django.utils.safestring.mark_safe on dynamic data. Disabling the framework's escaping layer makes every subsequent interpolation an XSS candidate.

rules.name: Response body written with dynamic HTML
rules.description: An HTTP response body is produced by interpolating values into an HTML string, for example with an f-string or concatenation passed to Response()/HttpResponse()/make_response(). The response declares HTML content type, so interpolated data executes as markup in the browser.
